title: H1 doesn't hold. The markdown rise isn't an R-410A clearance: it's a fixed price-down schedule on discontinued equipment SKUs that Hartwell keeps restocking, and only $4,059,115 of the 2022-2025 rise lands on prices
conclusion: The hypothesis fails on its main claim. Two of its side predictions do hold: no markdowns outside equipment, and none that vary by channel or order-taker. Every equipment markdown follows one rule: 2.1% a month after the SKU's discontinued_on date, capped at 42% from month 20. Within every cohort-month the rate is identical on every line, with no zero-markdown exceptions (q150). The discontinued SKUs come in three cohorts. The cohort dated 2015-01-01 and the one dated 2023-01-01 each split evenly: 44 R-410A, 44 R-454B and 44 non-refrigerant SKUs. Only the cohort dated 2025-01-01 is refrigerant-specific: 129 R-410A SKUs (q145). The recorded markdown also overstates the money. On special-order and transfer lines markdown_pct is set but the price isn't reduced: price-to-list is 0.8268 on marked special lines in 2025 against 0.8274 on unmarked ones (q171). Only stock lines carry a real price cut. Counting stock lines only, markdown dollars went from $1,320,450 in 2022 to $5,379,566 in 2025, an increase of $4,059,115 (q174, q180). The other $6,620,818 of 2025 recorded markdown sits on non-stock lines whose price wasn't cut (q174). In 2025 the 2023 cohort accounts for $3,454,074 of real markdown: $980,654 on R-410A, $1,069,154 on R-454B and $1,404,266 on non-refrigerant SKUs. The R-410A 2025 cohort accounts for $644,487 (q174, q180). The R-410A share of real markdown dollars only moved from 0.3005 to 0.372 (q180). The 2015 and 2023 cohorts aren't being cleared. They are bought again every year on stock POs: 2,720 units of the 2015 cohort and 6,699 of the 2023 cohort in 2025 (q160). They are then sold from stock at up to 42% off, which is below the (static) cost on all 2,497 + 6,126 such stock lines in 2025 (q165). Action: decide whether those SKUs are really discontinued. If they are, stop restocking them. If they aren't, clear or reset discontinued_on so the price rule stops marking them down. The 2025 stock-line markdown on these restocked cohorts is $4,735,079 a year (q180). That is the money at stake, not a proven saving.

claims.text: Markdowns appear only on equipment, every year 2016-2025. Parts, refrigeration and supplies have zero marked-down lines in every year. Equipment markdowns were already present before the transition, split across R-410A, R-454B and non-refrigerant SKUs, e.g. 2022 (recorded formula): $1,273,220 / $1,494,809 / $1,368,773, and 2016: $848,339 / $877,080 / $1,083,303.

The markdown is set by months since discontinued_on: 0.021 at month 1, rising 0.021 a month to 0.42 at month 20 and after. min = max in every cohort-month, and no line on a discontinued SKU after its date has a zero markdown. So it can't differ by channel, order-taker, account manager or customer.

There are three discontinued cohorts of marked-down SKUs: 2015-01-01 (44 R-410A, 44 R-454B, 44 none), 2023-01-01 (44/44/44) and 2025-01-01 (129 R-410A). Equipment SKUs never marked down are 130 R-454B and 130 non-refrigerant SKUs with no discontinued_on, plus 1 R-410A SKU.

markdown_pct cuts the price only on stock lines. In 2025, marked stock lines sell at 0.5507 of list against 0.8284 unmarked. Marked special lines sell at 0.8268 against 0.8274, and transfer lines at 0.8334 against 0.8319. The same pattern holds in 2016 and 2022. Recorded markdown on non-stock lines that never reached the price was $6,620,818 in 2025.

Markdown on stock lines (the real price cut) was $1,320,450 in 2022 and $5,379,566 in 2025, a rise of $4,059,115. The 2015 cohort held flat ($1,320,450 in 2022, $1,281,005 in 2025). The 2023 cohort added $3,454,074 and the R-410A 2025 cohort $644,487.

In 2025 the 2023 cohort's real markdown was $980,654 on R-410A, $1,069,154 on R-454B and $1,404,266 on non-refrigerant SKUs. The R-410A share of all real markdown dollars was 0.3005 in 2022 and 0.372 in 2025.

Discontinued SKUs keep being purchased. In 2025 there were stock POs for 2,720 units ($2,856,659) of the 2015 cohort and 6,699 units ($7,518,934) of the 2023 cohort, plus 2,785 and 3,257 special POs. Only the R-410A 2025 cohort's buying fell, from 10,326 stock units in 2024 to 582 in 2025.
In 2025 every stock line of the 2015 cohort (2,497) and of the 2023 cohort (6,126) sold below the static unit cost. Their gross margin was -$767,211.39 and -$2,022,425.19.

not_evidence_of: That anyone priced these lines by hand or kept them discounted for particular customers: the rate is mechanical and identical within each SKU-month. Also not evidence that all recorded 2025 markdown was given away: $6,620,818 of it sits on special and transfer lines whose price wasn't reduced. Below-cost margins use today's product cost (static, orient q41), so their size over time is uncertain.
could_not_tell: What discontinued_on means to the business (vendor end-of-life, or a pricing flag) and why discontinued SKUs are still bought. Whether these SKUs would sell at full price without the markdown, so how much of the at-risk amount could actually be kept. Why the markdown flag doesn't reach the price on special and transfer lines (a pricing-system behaviour, or a recording artefact). Historical costs, needed for true margin. Answering these would take the product lifecycle and pricing-rule configuration, vendor end-of-life notices and cost history.
next_step: Get the 264 SKUs in the 2015 and 2023 cohorts from erp_products and review them with purchasing and pricing. For each one, either stop replenishment, or correct discontinued_on so the 2.1%-a-month rule stops applying. Separately, ask how markdown_pct is meant to work on special and transfer lines, and correct the markdown reporting (q103) to count stock lines only.
dead_ends: Comparing markdown rates by channel, taken_by and account manager: moot, because the rate is fixed per SKU-month (q150), so there was nothing to compare.
Stock-age test (WMS running balance): not run, because the discontinued cohorts are restocked every year (q160), so aging stock can't explain the markdowns.
My own prediction that R-454B and non-refrigerant markdowns would tie to aged SKUs: they tie to discontinued_on cohorts, not to age of stock.
